## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trial results yet. The starting architecture scores 0.000 on both seeds, so the first goal is any nonzero success. From the code: input has 4Z+3 channels and already includes missing, extra and height channels. Actions are type-major, type × (Y·X) anchors, then DONE. The starting network already has a spatial pooling head, so the cause of zero success is probably too few samples and too few updates, or a weak footprint-aware head. Cutting PPO epochs gives up to about 3.25x more samples, but only while the network's compute ratio r stays near 1. So I keep the new architecture at r of about 1.2. The plan has three parts. A puts the new recipe on the starting network and tests the recipe alone. B uses a footprint-convolution head with residual blocks and normalisation under the same recipe, so A vs B tests the architecture. C is B with 2 epochs and lower entropy, so B vs C tests the epoch count.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 in training success on both seeds. That covers 1 or 2 PPO epochs, entropy 0.003–0.005, gamma 0.99, and both the pooling head and the footprint-conv head. Every run took about 67 s, far below the 900 s cap. Getting zero even in training, with these partial-fill rewards, suggests a structural mismatch rather than too few samples. The likeliest cause is that this world differs from its description: a fully convolutional head assumes action index a maps to cell (y, x) of the observation. If the real layout is transposed, flipped or shifted, a 3x3 conv stack with a small receptive field cannot learn the mapping. Round 2 therefore tests heads that do not depend on the action layout. Candidate 1 replaces the conv head with a flat MLP head, candidate 2 adds a flat correction branch to B's conv head, and candidate 3 is a plain MLP on the raw observation and mask. All three keep the 1-epoch recipe, so their results compare directly with round 1's B.

### Round 3
All 7 trials scored 0. That covers the starting net, the footprint-conv head, two flat-MLP heads and a plain MLP, run with 1 or 2 PPO epochs and several entropy settings. Training success was also 0 everywhere, so no seed produced any signal, and the noise figure cannot separate the trials. The MLP needs no layout assumptions and still failed, so a mismatch between the action layout and the grid is an unlikely cause. The more likely cause is that learning is too hard: the net must find the landing layer (the highest filled cell under the brick's footprint) and match it to target cells at exactly that layer. No net so far has a direct path for that. The recipe also allows only about 2–3k gradient steps in total, about 100 updates × 32 minibatches. Next I test a head that scores each placement per layer, with a learned soft choice of landing layer. I also test whether more gradient steps help.

### Round 4
After 9 trials, every candidate scores exactly 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That includes the starting network, footprint-conv heads, a per-layer landing head, flat-MLP heads and a plain MLP. Recipe changes made no difference either: 1 or 2 epochs, entropy 0.003–0.005, doubled gradient steps. When even training success stays at 0 everywhere, the cause is more likely a mismatch between the network and the world than a lack of samples. The task warns that the world may differ from its description. One likely mismatch is that the action index-to-cell mapping, or the anchor corner, differs from the documented layout. If so, every spatial head would score the wrong cells. The flat heads can learn any mapping but are too slow on this budget. This is the last round, so I hedge: one conv network, one output head for each of the 8 board rotations and reflections, each read out in 2 orders (type-first or cell-first). The 16 heads' logits are summed. Gradient should select the matching head, and 3x3 output kernels absorb anchor offsets of one cell.
